subtopic: Hedge Funds vs. Registered Investment Funds
source_evidence: Hedge funds generally pursue more flexible investments and strategies than registered investment companies, like mutual funds and ETFs, which may increase the risk of investment losses. They are not subject to the numerous regulations that apply to mutual funds and ETFs for the protection of investors
answer: Hedge funds are private, unregistered investment funds, while mutual funds and ETFs are examples of registered investment companies. Hedge funds generally have more flexibility in their investments and strategies, which may increase the risk of losses. They also do not have to follow many of the investor-protection regulations that apply to mutual funds and ETFs. For example, mutual fund shares must be redeemable daily based on net asset value; hedge funds may limit when investors can redeem their shares.
